clue.text: Grace, opening batsman, gets unusual singles

parts.note: the first letter of the word batsman opens it

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of singles are put into an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: W.G. Grace, opening the batting, picks up an odd run of singles.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes W.G. Grace, the famous English cricketer, so 'Grace' looks like a name; it is the definition, a prayer before meals.
explanation.definitionFit: A grace said before a meal is a blessing asked over the food.

clue.text: Unauthorised demand for suspension

parts.note: suspension suggests a school or job penalty, but here means hanging by a mob without legal trial

explanation.surface: An improper call for someone to be suspended from work.
explanation.definitionFit: Mob justice punishing a supposed offender, often by hanging, without lawful trial.

clue.text: Making oneself barely visible?

parts.note: barely visible suggests hardly seen, but means visible in a bare state, having removed clothes

explanation.surface: Someone trying to stay inconspicuous.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing one's clothes leaves one naked.

clue.text: The opposite of a sun-bonnet?

parts.note: a sun-bonnet is headwear against heat; its opposite is a frozen covering, as on a polar summit

explanation.surface: Asking what the reverse of a summer hat would be.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent frozen sheet covering the polar regions or a mountain top.

clue.text: He's very stupid to continue

explanation.surface: A slow-witted man urged to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimwitted fool; and, as two words, a phrase meaning to carry on.

clue.text: Movement of finger, making a bid

indicators.note: movement suggests the letters of of finger are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: At an auction, a twitch of the finger signals a bid.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting forward a price or proposal is tendering, as at an auction.

clue.text: Generator is mounted by engineers

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means going up, so the word is is written upwards

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps

explanation.surface: A power generator is installed by a team of engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'mounted' means written upwards, so the word 'is' climbs before the engineers' abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A father, especially of a horse, is the one who begets offspring.

clue.text: People correspond, but not physically

parts.note: men means people in the general sense
to tally is to match or agree

explanation.surface: People agree with one another, but only in spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in the mind rather than with the body.

clue.text: Stroke of a cricketer, starting on a run?

parts.note: runners at the start of a race are said to be off
a run out in the car is a drive

explanation.surface: A batsman sets off on a run as soon as he plays his shot.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a drive struck to the off side of the field is a standard batting shot.

clue.text: Have to make a return to divorce city, a heavy blow

indicators.note: making a return means going back, so the city name is read backwards

parts.note: Reno in Nevada was famous for quick divorces

explanation.surface: Someone forced to go back to Reno for a divorce suffers a crushing setback.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is British slang for a single mighty punch, one that needs no follow-up.

clue.text: Of Peruvian ancestry? Brilliant!

parts.note: the Incas were the ancient people of Peru, so Incan means of Peruvian origin
descent means lineage or ancestry

explanation.surface: Someone delighted to learn their forebears came from Peru.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as an exclamation of delight, but its first half is a punning phrase about Peruvian heritage, and only 'Brilliant' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Something glowing with white heat shines dazzlingly, so the word is used for anything dazzling.

clue.text: React badly to girl having a free hand

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of react are put into a disordered form

parts.note: Blanche is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl allowed to do as she likes reacts poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns REACT into CARTE, followed by BLANCHE.
explanation.definitionFit: French for blank card: complete freedom to act as one sees fit.

clue.text: House buzzer may be stuck on here

definitions.text: House buzzer may be stuck on here

parts.words: House buzzer may be stuck on here
parts.note: the house buzzer is not a doorbell but the common housefly, which gets trapped on a sticky strip

explanation.surface: A doorbell button that has been glued in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticky strips are hung in homes to trap insects such as houseflies.

clue.text: A subject causing trouble?

parts.note: subject suggests a topic of discussion, but means a monarch's subject who rises against the ruler

explanation.surface: A contentious topic of conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rises in revolt against the established authority.

clue.text: Republic is to bring back a king

indicators.note: bringing something back turns it round, so the king's name is read backwards

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A republic plans to restore a monarch to the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: The Middle Eastern state is a parliamentary republic, an example of the category.

clue.text: A child of two

parts.note: reads like a toddler aged two, but means one child out of a pair born together

explanation.surface: A two-year-old toddler.
explanation.definitionFit: One of a pair of siblings born at the same birth.

clue.text: He paints badly so becomes an actor

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of he paints are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who is a poor painter turns to the stage instead.
explanation.definitionFit: From Thespis, legendary Greek founder of tragedy: a performer on stage.

clue.text: Clear a computer program?

parts.note: clearing here means removing errors from the code, with a hint of removing insects

explanation.surface: An instruction to wipe software off a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Programmers remove faults, traditionally called bugs, from code before release.

clue.text: He takes part in an act of duplicity

definitions.text: He takes part in an act of duplicity

parts.words: He takes part in an act of duplicity
parts.note: duplicity suggests deceit, but here means doubleness: a performance by two

explanation.surface: A man who joins in a deception.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer in a piece for two musicians or singers.

clue.text: Extrasensory perception you start to detect

parts.note: ESP is the abbreviation for extrasensory perception

indicators.note: start points to the opening letter of the word you

explanation.surface: Psychic powers help you begin to sense things.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot or catch sight of something is to notice or discover it.

clue.text: Poem completed but not written down

parts.note: past means over and done
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A poem finished but never committed to paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural idyll in verse, about shepherds and country life.

clue.text: What the unsatisfied audience may shout

definitions.text: What the unsatisfied audience may shout

parts.words: What the unsatisfied audience may shout
parts.note: unsatisfied suggests discontent, but this audience has simply not had enough and wants more

explanation.surface: Disgruntled theatregoers heckling the performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A French call for a repeat performance, shouted by fans wanting more.

clue.text: Uninterested, having no inclination either way

explanation.surface: Someone indifferent with no preference in any direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads LIST as a lean or tilt, as a ship lists, so a ship with no list is upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathetic and lacking energy; also, read literally, without any tilt to either side.

clue.text: Remarkable way to communicate

explanation.surface: An extraordinary method of getting a message across.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, notable or striking; as a noun, a gesture or sign sending a message.

clue.text: The difference between buying and selling

definitions.text: The difference between buying and selling

parts.words: The difference between buying and selling
parts.note: reads as a contrast of two activities, but means the money gap between cost price and sale price

explanation.surface: A philosophical musing on what separates purchase from sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader's gain is the gap between what goods cost and what they fetch.

clue.text: Marks dropped in proper examination

indicators.note: dropped means a piece is left out

parts.note: moral means proper or virtuous
M stands for marks, the former German currency

explanation.surface: Points lost in a fair test.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as in a language exam or thesis defence.

clue.text: It's wrapped up by postal sorters, too

indicators.note: wrapped up by means enclosed within the words postal sorters

explanation.surface: A parcel bundled up by workers in the mail office.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in addition or as well.

clue.text: Short cut that's about right

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shortcut that is roughly correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A brusque reply is abrupt, using as few words as possible.

clue.text: They should be able to identify any salts in a mixture

definitions.text: They should be able to identify any salts in a mixture

indicators.note: letters in a mixture are jumbled, so any and salts are rearranged together

explanation.surface: Chemists ought to be able to spot whatever salts are in a compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mixture' rearranges ANY SALTS; the whole clue is also the definition of chemists who test substances.
explanation.definitionFit: Laboratory chemists test samples to determine their composition.

clue.text: Will lose varied sources of mineral deposits

indicators.note: varied means altered, so the letters of will lose are rearranged

explanation.surface: A will may forfeit assorted mining interests.
explanation.definitionFit: Petroleum, a mineral oil, is pumped up from bores sunk into the ground.
